correctness.rationale: Independent exact replay in Python (numpy 1.26.4, sympy 1.12) confirms every essential inference. Gerzon: ((1-a2)I+a2J) with a=1/3 has eigenvalues 8/9 and 8/9+n/9>0, hence invertible, so v_i v_i^T are independent in Sym_d; d(d+1)/2 gives 21,28,36 for d=6,7,8. Relative (trace) bound: n^2=(sum lambda)^2<=d sum lambda^2=d tr(G^2) with tr(G^2)=n+n(n-1)/9 gives n(1-d/9)<=d(8/9); for d=6,7 yields 16,28 exactly; d=8 gives 64 (weaker than Gerzon). Delsarte LP: verified via sympy gegenbauer with lambda=(d-2)/2 that P2=(6t^2-1)/5 (d=6), (7t^2-1)/6 (d=7), P4=(40t^4-20t^2+1)/21 (d=8); exact rational identities 18t^2-2=1+15P2, (63t^2-7)/2=1+27P2, (3240t^4-1620t^2+140)/59=1+(1701/59)P4 all have diff 0, f(1)=16,28,1760/59=29.8305, f(+/-1/3)=0<=0, coefficients >=0, so Delsarte (cited as black box, standard Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1977) gives n<=16,28,29 integrally; hand-checked 3240/59 etc. match; exhaustive even-k check to degree 60 confirms k=4 is best single-polynomial LP bound for d=8 (k=2 gives 64, k>=6 give >=82; odd k alone impossible since 1+cv<=0 and 1-cv<=0 cannot both hold). Witnesses: loaded both CSVs, verified symmetric, diag {3}, off alphabet {1,-1}, trace 48/84 and sum 128/0 matching draft; rebuilt Clebsch from 4-bit Hamming {1,4} (degree 5, SRG(16,5,0,2) verified: adjacent 0, nonadjacent 2 common neighbours) and T8 from 28 two-subsets intersecting in 1 (degree 12) with M=3I+S / 3I-S respectively, both equal saved matrices exactly; independent Fractions LDL with max-diag pivoting gives pivots [3,8/3,5/2,12/5,4/3,1] rank 6 and [3,8/3,5/2,12/5,7/3,16/7,9/4] rank 7 with remaining Schur exactly zero; float eigvalsh min -2.3e-15/-5.5e-15 (>= -1e-8), 10/21 near-zero, max 8.0/12.0 consistent. Nonextendability: rebuilt u_i=e_i-1/8*1 (Gram 7/8 diag, -1/8 off), w=u/sqrt(7/8) (1 diag, -1/7 off), v_ij=sqrt(2/3)(u_i+u_j) Gram is 1 diag and +1/3 if share / -1/3 if disjoint, max|Gv-Gsaved|=3.4e-16; decomposition x=(y,t) with y in 7-dim span covers any ambient dimension (t=0 allowed); |z_i+z_j|=sqrt(12/7)/3=2/sqrt(21)=c verified; identity sum_{i<j}(z_i+z_j)^2=6 sum z_i^2 under sum z=0 verified on random vectors (each square in 7 pairs, cross term -S2/2); S2=28c^2/6=8/9 exact (c^2=4/21); quantization 2z_i/c=s_ij+s_ik-s_jk in {-3,-1,1,3} enumerated; S2/a^2 with a^2=1/21 is 56/3 non-integer, contradiction; norm (7/8)S2=7/9<=1 consistent but unneeded. Frontier honesty verified: no n=29 closure claimed; small-n blowup and 2^28 barrier quantified. Proofs are exact rational arithmetic, not experimental; frontier timing is experimental but not used for theorems. All scripts replay without failure.

originality.rationale: Live retrieval (arXiv abs pages + Crossref API + DOI/publisher pages, 2026-09-07) finds nearest priors are different strata/methods and do not state the same certified table with same pipeline. Jiang et al. 1907.12466 proves large-d formula N_{1/3}(d)=2d-2 for sufficiently large d via sublinear second-eigenvalue multiplicity, explicitly not settling small d=6-8 where sporadic 28 exceeds the line. Lin-Yu 1807.06249 proves Lemmens-Seidel 1/5 claims via pillar/two-graph uniqueness and determines maxima for r=8,9,10 unrestricted, different angle (1/5 vs 1/3) and non-computational method. de Laat et al. 2211.16471 computes Lasserre levels 2-3 for asymptotic SDP bounds, no per-dimension Gram witnesses or infeasibility logs for d=6-8 at 1/3. Greaves et al. 1403.2155 improves unrestricted maxima in d=14,16 via Seidel enumeration and corrects tables, different stratum (unrestricted N(d) vs fixed N_{1/3}(d)). Barg-Yu 2014 (Contemp. Math. 625) improves SDP bounds for 24<=n<=136 and Delsarte 1977 / Lemmens-Seidel 1973 provide methods, but no retrieved record exhibits the specific table N=16,28 plus 28-29 interval plus T8 inclusion-maximality with exact rational LDL/Cholesky replay and explicit Delsarte polynomial 1760/59 for this stratum. Syatriadi 2026 thesis determines unrestricted N(14)=28 etc., different stratum. Kao-Yu SSRN 2026 four-point SDP abstract claims uniqueness for 7<=d<=14 at 1/3, which would subsume N(8), but only the abstract was retrievable via Crossref (full SSRN blocked), it is an unrefereed preprint deposited May 2026, and its proof was not inspected, so it is noted as residual risk, not decisive anticipation. Authors honestly concede 16,28 follow from classical relative bound plus known Clebsch/T8 and may be handbook-tabulated; originality therefore rests narrowly on the tightened d=8 LP certificate with exact identity plus the elementary any-dimension nonextendability theorem plus machine-checkable witnesses, none of which was found in inspected priors.

value.rationale: Motivated small-d gap where asymptotic 2d-2 fails and sporadic 28 lives; not arbitrary parameter fixation. While N=16,28 alone follow from textbook relative bound plus well-known graphs (authors concede), the unit as a whole goes beyond restatement: (i) fully machine-checkable certification with integer Gram matrices, exact pivot lists, exact polynomial identities and stdlib+numpy+sympy replay in seconds (sha-verified), (ii) non-trivial tightening for d=8 from Gerzon 36 to 29 via explicit degree-4 Delsarte certificate 1760/59, verified best single-polynomial LP bound to degree 60 among evens (19% reduction, narrowing open N(8) to {28,29}), and (iii) new elementary structural theorem that the 28-set is inclusion-maximal in any dimension (56/3 quantization, not just cardinality maximality in R7, and explicitly not claiming to rule out a different 29-set, honestly leaving 28-vs-29 open with quantified search barrier). Together with honest limitations, conjecture, and frontier quantification, this is a solid bounded-census unit independently worth finding later by workers on spherical codes/equiangular lines who need replayable small-stratum witnesses and the narrowest explicit LP upper bound short of full SDP closure. Not a tiny unmotivated gain, not an unexplained enumeration.

queries.query: Equiangular lines with a fixed angle

sources.comparison: Proves N_alpha(d)=floor(k(d-1)/(k-1)) for fixed alpha in all sufficiently large d via sublinear second-eigenvalue multiplicity; for alpha=1/3 gives 2d-2 asymptotically. Provides no exact certified small-dimension census for d=6-8 with exhaustive Gram witnesses, exact rational Cholesky/rank certificates, or tightened LP 29 bound and nonextendability proof; complementary large-d theory.
sources.title: Equiangular lines with a fixed angle

sources.comparison: Proves Lemmens-Seidel 1973 angle-1/5 claims via pillar decompositions and 276-vertex two-graph uniqueness, determining exact unrestricted maxima for r=8,9,10. Different angle stratum (1/5 vs fixed 1/3 in R6-R8) and different certifying method; no PSD-constrained Gram backtracking with absolute/relative LP plus exact Cholesky replay for d=6-8 at 1/3.
sources.title: Equiangular lines and the Lemmens-Seidel conjecture

sources.comparison: Computes Lasserre hierarchy levels 2-3 for spherical finite-distance problems to obtain new asymptotic linear SDP bounds on fixed-angle equiangular lines. Provides hierarchy analysis and representation-theoretic computation, not per-dimension exact maximal cardinalities with explicit Gram witnesses and pruned-search logs for d=6-8 at alpha=1/3.
sources.title: The Lasserre hierarchy for equiangular lines with a fixed angle

sources.comparison: Obtains new general lower bounds, classifies two-graphs on 12 vertices, studies Seidel matrices with three eigenvalues, and improves unrestricted maxima in dimensions 14 and 16 while correcting literature tables. Concerns unrestricted N(d), not the fixed-angle stratum N_{1/3}(6-8), and uses Seidel enumeration rather than LP-pruned Gram certification with Delsarte 1760/59 and 56/3 nonextendability.
sources.title: Equiangular lines in Euclidean spaces

sources.comparison: Foundational Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel linear-programming method for spherical codes (Gegenbauer positivity, f(1)/f0 bound) cited as black box in the draft. Provides the general theorem, not the specific degree-4 certificate (3240t^4-1620t^2+140)/59 giving 1760/59 for d=8 at alpha=1/3 nor the Clebsch/T8 exact witnesses.
sources.title: Spherical codes and designs

residual_risks: Small-d values 16,28 follow directly from classical relative bound plus known Clebsch/T8; authors concede possible handbook tabulation (Barg-Yu tables, Syatriadi thesis). No retrieved table was inspected proving prior explicit statement, but re-certification value depends on machine-checkability, not first discovery.

Kao-Yu SSRN 2026 four-point SDP preprint (Crossref DOI 10.2139/ssrn.6726772, abstract only inspected) claims uniqueness for 7<=d<=14 at alpha=1/3, which if verified would subsume the 28-vs-29 gap and T8 maximality with a stronger result; full text not retrieved (SSRN blocked), unrefereed, so not decisive but could obsolete the interval.

Delsarte LP positivity (sum P_k >=0) cited not reproved; statement matches standard Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1977 as verified via DOI record, but audit did not re-derive representation theory; misstatement would invalidate upper bounds, though polynomial identities themselves are exact.

Barg-Yu 2013/2014 SDP bounds may already imply <=29 for d=8 at 1/3 with stronger machinery; comparison to those tables not performed beyond abstracts, so 36->29 improvement is over Gerzon baseline only.

Float cross-checks use tolerances 1e-8/1e-6; exact Fractions LDL already proves PSD/rank, so floats are secondary, but pivoted-Cholesky second implementation shares float rounding risk (agreement observed).
N_{1/3}(8) remains open (28 vs 29); conjecture N=28 is unproved and a non-T8 29-set is not ruled out; future SDP/Seidel classification could close or overturn the interval.
